key_insight: For consumer IMU-based pose estimation, the main bottleneck is not just noisy sensors overall, but unreliability at the channel level. The paper shows that selectively trusting and fusing only the most reliable head and foot IMU signals can improve lower-body 3D pose estimation.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of estimating accurate lower-body 3D pose from sparse consumer IMUs when sensor orientations are biased, mounting differs across sessions, and data may drift or drop out.
method: Builds a new 35-take single-subject benchmark using an earbud head IMU and two smart-insole foot IMUs with SAM-3D-Body pseudo-ground-truth labels.
Performs channel-level reliability analysis via ablation to identify which IMU signals contribute trustworthy motion information, especially foot acceleration.
Uses reliability-gated fusion to combine only dependable sensor channels for more robust lower-body pose estimation.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests that better results may come from modeling sensor reliability explicitly rather than treating all IMU channels equally. It provides a practical path toward more robust camera-free motion capture on consumer hardware.
visual_elements: System diagram showing head IMU and two foot IMUs feeding into a reliability-gated fusion model.
Channel ablation chart comparing performance when individual IMU channels are removed.
Data pipeline graphic from raw IMU streams to fused lower-body 3D pose output.
Side-by-side pose visualization comparing baseline vs reliability-gated predictions.
paper_title: Reliability-Gated Fusion of Consumer Head and Foot IMUs for Lower-Body 3D Pose
paper_authors: Zhilin Guo, Boqiao Zhang, Oszkár Urbán, Josef Bengtson, Hakan Aktas
